subject: Numeracy
title: One and lots
objectives: Children will take or show one when asked.
Children will tell one thing from lots of things.
content: The idea of one, lots, a few and none, using real objects and counting games.
teachingActivities: Use "one" firmly in routines: give one cup, one biscuit; use "lots" when there are many; use "all gone" for none.
learnerActivities: Take one object, show lots, give one to a friend, and say "all gone" when none are left.
resources: Baskets of beads in large sizes (wooden blocks, large buttons)
assessment: Observe whether each child can give or take one when asked and tell one from lots.
expectedOutcomes: Gives exactly one object on request.
Uses the word one or lots.
crossCurricular: Literacy: one, lots and all gone in rhymes
Social Habits: sharing and giving one to a friend
Physical Development: picking up and passing objects

lessons.title: Give me one
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will take one object when asked.
successCriteria: Takes exactly one object on request
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort and compare by size and say some words such as big, small and same.
lessons.starter: Hold up one finger and say "One!" Take one block from the basket and say "I have one block."
teacherActivities: Say "Give me one block" and hold out your hand.
Say "Thank you. One block." Ask another child.
Show lots of blocks and ask "Can you take one?"
learnerActivities: Child takes one block and gives it to you.
Each child takes one block and puts it on the tray.
Child takes one and keeps the others in the basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "Give me one block" and hold out your hand. Children: Child takes one block and gives it to you.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Thank you. One block." Ask another child. Children: Each child takes one block and puts it on the tray.
Step 3. Teacher: Show lots of blocks and ask "Can you take one?" Children: Child takes one and keeps the others in the basket.

practical.title: One for the tray
steps: Place a basket of blocks in front of the group.
Each child puts one block on the tray.
practical.safety: Use large wooden or plastic blocks that cannot be swallowed. Supervise at all times.

differentiation.support: Offer a basket of only two blocks and say "one" as you place the first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to take one block in each hand and say "two".

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many blocks did you take?

lessons.conclusion: Put all the single blocks into a line and say "One, one, one." Clap.
lessons.homeConnection: At snack time, ask your child to take one biscuit or one spoon.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "take one object when asked" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: One finger, one finger, one finger up. One block, one block, one block up.

lessons.title: Lots and a few
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will tell lots from a few using real objects.
successCriteria: Points to the group with lots
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort and compare by size and say some words such as big, small and same.
resources: Two baskets: one with many large blocks, one with two or three
lessons.starter: Show a basket with lots of blocks and a basket with a few. Say "Lots! A few!" using different hand gestures.
teacherActivities: Pour out lots of blocks and say "Lots of blocks!" Pour out a few and say "A few."
Ask "Which has lots?" and "Which has a few?"
Let each child take a few and put the rest back.
learnerActivities: Children point to each pile and say "lots" or "few".
Children point to the right pile.
Child takes two or three blocks.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pour out lots of blocks and say "Lots of blocks!" Pour out a few and say "A few." Children: Children point to each pile and say "lots" or "few".
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which has lots?" and "Which has a few?" Children: Children point to the right pile.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child take a few and put the rest back. Children: Child takes two or three blocks.

practical.title: Lots and few piles
steps: Ask them to make a pile with lots and a pile with a few.
Check by pointing to each pile.
practical.safety: Use only large blocks and keep the area clear. Supervise to prevent mouthing.

differentiation.support: Offer one block and a basket full of blocks, which is an obvious difference.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell you how many are in the few pile by counting.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Sweep the piles together and say "Lots of blocks, tidy up!"
lessons.homeConnection: At home, show your child lots of spoons and a few spoons and talk about them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "tell lots from a few using real objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: All gone!
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say "all gone" when no objects are left.
successCriteria: Notices when a container is empty
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort and compare by size and say some words such as big, small and same.
lessons.starter: Pretend to eat toy fruits one by one. After each, say "One, gobble!" until the basket is empty. Say "All gone!" and show your empty hands.
teacherActivities: Place a few fruits in a basket and let a child take them out one by one.
When the basket is empty, say "All gone!" and open your hands.
Hide a toy under a cloth and ask "Is it there? All gone?" Lift the cloth to reveal.
learnerActivities: Child takes each fruit and puts it in the bag.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place a few fruits in a basket and let a child take them out one by one. Children: Child takes each fruit and puts it in the bag.
Step 2. Teacher: When the basket is empty, say "All gone!" and open your hands. Children: Children copy with open hands.
Step 3. Teacher: Hide a toy under a cloth and ask "Is it there? All gone?" Lift the cloth to reveal. Children: Children say "all gone" or "there!".

practical.title: Fruit basket game
steps: Each child has a small basket of three toy fruits.
They take them out one by one.
They say "all gone" when the basket is empty.
practical.safety: Use toy fruits larger than a child’s fist. Do not use real small fruits or sweets.

differentiation.support: Use a basket with one object.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say how many were in the basket at the start.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is in the basket now?
Can you say all gone?
questions.expected: Child says or signs all gone.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the empty basket. Say "All gone!" together.
lessons.homeConnection: Say "all gone" at mealtimes when the plate is empty.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say "all gone" when no objects are left" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: One for you
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will give one object to a friend.
successCriteria: Gives one object to a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort and compare by size and say some words such as big, small and same.
resources: A basket of large biscuits or toy biscuits
lessons.starter: Say "Teddy is hungry! Can you give Teddy one biscuit?" Hold out the basket.
teacherActivities: Give one toy biscuit to Teddy and say "One biscuit for Teddy."
Invite a child to give one biscuit to each soft toy.
Say "Now one for you" and give each child one.
learnerActivities: Child gives one biscuit and says "one".
Child takes one and says "thank you".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give one toy biscuit to Teddy and say "One biscuit for Teddy." Children: Children watch and say "one".
Step 2. Teacher: Invite a child to give one biscuit to each soft toy. Children: Child gives one biscuit and says "one".
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Now one for you" and give each child one. Children: Child takes one and says "thank you".

practical.title: One for the toys
steps: Seat soft toys in a row.
Each child gives one toy biscuit to a toy.
Check that each toy has one.
practical.safety: Use toy biscuits or large safe items. If using real food, check for allergies and wash hands first.

differentiation.support: Use one toy and one biscuit.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give one to each of three toys.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many biscuits does Teddy have?

lessons.conclusion: Sing "One for you, one for me" and tidy the toys away.
lessons.homeConnection: At mealtimes, hand out one spoon or plate to each person.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "give one object to a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: One and lots stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show one, lots and all gone at three stations.
successCriteria: Tells lots from few and says all gone
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort and compare by size and say some words such as big, small and same.
lessons.starter: Sing the "One finger" song and show the stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask observed children to take one, show lots and say all gone.
Record each child’s level and photograph.
learnerActivities: Child takes one, points to lots and says all gone.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask observed children to take one, show lots and say all gone. Children: Child takes one, points to lots and says all gone.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and photograph. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Remove small items and supervise all stations.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a friend in the game.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: gives one; tells lots from few; says all gone.

questions.question: Which has lots?
questions.expected: Child points to the larger group.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
lessons.conclusion: Sing the "One finger" song again and tidy up.
lessons.homeConnection: Count one object a day at home and say "one".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show one, lots and all gone at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
